```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 0.3)

# draws n full-width blank lines (margin to margin) for handwritten answers,
# as a single plot so spacing is deterministic; pair with fig.height = 0.3 * n
blank_lines <- function(n = 1) {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, n), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    segments(0, n - i + 0.5, 1, n - i + 0.5, lwd = 1)
  }
}

# keeps a prompt and its answer space on one PDF page: place `r nq(...)` on its
# own line just above the prompt. Emits nothing in non-LaTeX output. lines =
# lines of prompt text, rows = rows of blank space below it (0.3 in each),
# extra = any other height (in inches), e.g. a figure
nq <- function(lines, rows = 0, extra = 0) {
  if (!knitr::is_latex_output()) return("")
  knitr::asis_output(sprintf("\n\\needspace{%.2fin}\n", 0.23 * lines + 0.15 + 0.3 * rows + extra))
}
```

**NRES 746, Week 8, Lecture 1: How Much Did the Prior Matter?**

Name: ___________________________________________

**Instructions:** Work alone on Part 1 (about 4 minutes), then compare
with a neighbor for Part 2. Keep laptops closed.

## The study

A biologist radio-tracks juvenile desert tortoises at one site and
records which ones survive the year. Three analysts estimate annual
survival from the **same data**, but each chooses a different prior:

- **Analyst A** uses a weak prior centered on 0.5.
- **Analyst B** uses earlier estimates from juveniles raised in a
  predator-proof pen.
- **Analyst C** uses an estimate from a severe drought year at another
  site.

Each panel shows one analyst's prior (grey) and posterior (black). The
likelihood, which is the same in all three panels, is not shown.

```{r prior-post-panels, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=5.6}
s_seq <- seq(0.001, 0.999, length.out = 500)
survived <- 21
collared <- 30
priors <- list(A = c(2, 2), B = c(46, 4), C = c(10, 10))
par(mfrow = c(4, 1), mar = c(2.8, 4, 1.3, 0.5), mgp = c(1.8, 0.5, 0))
for (an in names(priors)) {
  pr <- priors[[an]]
  po <- pr + c(survived, collared - survived)
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 12), xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i",
       xlab = "Annual survival probability", ylab = "Density",
       main = paste("Analyst", an), cex.main = 1, font.main = 1)
  abline(v = seq(0, 1, 0.1), col = "grey90")
  lines(s_seq, dbeta(s_seq, pr[1], pr[2]), lwd = 2.5, col = "grey60")
  lines(s_seq, dbeta(s_seq, po[1], po[2]), lwd = 2.5)
  if (an == "A") {
    legend("topleft", c("prior", "posterior"), lwd = 2.5,
           col = c("grey60", "black"), bty = "n", cex = 0.9)
  }
  box()
}
plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 12), xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i", yaxt = "n",
     xlab = "Annual survival probability", ylab = "",
     main = "Your sketch: the shared likelihood", cex.main = 1, font.main = 1)
abline(v = seq(0, 1, 0.1), col = "grey90")
box()
```

`r nq(4, 3)`

## Part 1: Find the likelihood (individual)

**1a.** Sketch the shared likelihood on the bottom panel (the height
doesn't matter; get its peak and width roughly right). Which analyst's
panel did you rely on most, and why?

```{r fig.height=0.3*3}
blank_lines(3)
```

`r nq(3, 3)`

**1b.** Rank the three analysts' results from most to least dependent
on their choice of prior. Give a one-line reason for each.

```{r fig.height=0.3*3}
blank_lines(3)
```

`r nq(5, 4)`

## Part 2: Which number? (with a neighbor)

**2a.** The three posterior means for annual survival are 0.68 (A), 0.84
(B), and 0.62 (C). A manager needs one survival rate for a population
model. What would you tell them, and what would you report?

```{r fig.height=0.3*4}
blank_lines(4)
```
